positions.name: KnowledgeSuppressionDirective
positions.frame: how is knowledge suppression performed when a directive to remove is paired with a corrective claim about what never happened?
positions.why: All three expressions share one directional read: the speaker commands erasure of specific knowledge (Kestrelwood spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work) through paired imperatives, then supplies a flat corrective assertion that the observatory never performed the calibration. The set holds tension between the decision-level imperatives (src-1, src-2) and the claim-level assertion (src-3) — the directives demand compliance while the assertion provides the replacement narrative — but both sides cohere under the frame's read of how suppression is enacted through command and correction together.
